record.original_question: Is it possible to choose the domain so that the dynamics of the corresponding billiard map are locally (near the 2-periodic orbit) conjugated to th e dynamics of the rigid rotation through some angle α? V. Schastnyy and D. Treschev [199] provide numerical evidence th at this is possible if α/π is a Dio- phantine number. 4.2.2 Geometry of caustics, invariant surfaces, and commut ing billiard maps A p/q-rational caustic corresponds to an invariant circle of the billiard ma p that consists of periodic points with the rotation number p/q. For example, a curve of constant width has a 1 /2 caustic, the envelop of the 2-periodic, back and forth, billiard orbits. A Birkhoff in tegrable billiard has a family 16 of p/q-rational caustics for all sufficiently small values of p/q - this follows from the Arnold-Liouville theorem. An ellipse possesses p/q-rational caustics for all p/q < 1/2. Kaloshin and K. Zhang [128] proved that, in an appropriate topology, the set of Birkhoff billiards that possess a rational caustic is dense in the space of Birkhoff billiards. Baryshnikov and Zharnitsky [7] and Landsberg [145] used methods of exterior differential systems to construct infinite-dimensional families of billiards having a p/q-rational caustic for a fixed value of p/q; see [84] for outer billiards.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a smooth strictly convex planar domain, and let $T:\partial\Omega \times (0,\pi) \to \partial\Omega \times (0,\pi)$ be the associated Birkhoff billiard map (sending an inward-pointing unit vector based at a boundary point to the next such vector after elastic reflection at the boundary). A 2-periodic orbit of $T$ is a back-and-forth trajectory along a chord that meets $\partial\Omega$ orthogonally at both endpoints.

Fix $\alpha\in(0,\pi)$. The question is: does there exist a smooth strictly convex domain $\Omega$ possessing a 2-periodic billiard orbit $p$ such that, in some neighborhood of $p$ in phase space, the billiard map $T$ is (smoothly, or analytically) conjugate to the rigid rotation $R_\alpha$ of a disk by angle $\alpha$?

In particular, can such a smooth (or analytic) conjugacy be realized whenever $\alpha/\pi$ is Diophantine (i.e., there exist $C,\tau>0$ such that $|\alpha/\pi - p/q| \ge C q^{-\tau}$ for all integers $p,q$ with $q\ge 1$)?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is classical (Treschev). Formal power series solutions exist when α/π is irrational, and numerical evidence supports convergence for Diophantine α. Wang–Zhang (arXiv:2211.03182) proved Gevrey regularity of the Treschev formal solution under a Diophantine condition, but actual convergence (existence of a genuine smooth/analytic domain with the desired local conjugacy) remains open as of recent literature.

status_evidence.title: Gevrey regularity for the formally linearizable billiard of Treschev
status_evidence.snippet: If the frequency for the linear dynamics is Diophantine, the Treschev example is (1+α)-Gevrey for some α > 0.
status_evidence.claim: Only Gevrey regularity, not analyticity/convergence, has been established under Diophantine conditions; full conjugacy result remains open.

status_evidence.title: On Local Integrability in Billiard Dynamics
status_evidence.snippet: Schastnyy and Treschev: numerical evidence for convergence of the formal series for Diophantine α.
status_evidence.claim: Existence is supported numerically but not proven.

status_evidence.title: On a conjugacy problem in billiard dynamics
status_evidence.snippet: Treschev's formal series approach to the local conjugacy problem near a 2-periodic orbit.
status_evidence.claim: Formal power-series solutions exist; analytic existence is the open question.
